properties.name: Long Tank (Otteri Nullah)
properties.source: Care Earth Trust / IIT Madras Water Bodies Study
properties.notes: One of the largest tanks in central Chennai, the Long Tank once ran from Vepery to Otteri covering ~200 ha. Completely drained and built over during British colonial-era urban expansion. Now occupied by roads, housing and commercial buildings in Vepery-Otteri area.

properties.name: Nungambakkam Tank
properties.source: Survey of India historical maps / Chennai Metropolitan Development Authority
properties.notes: A major water tank that once occupied the Nungambakkam area. Drained during colonial expansion to develop what is now one of Chennai's most upscale residential and commercial neighbourhoods. No trace remains today.

properties.name: Kodambakkam Lake
properties.source: Care Earth Trust water body survey
properties.notes: Kodambakkam Lake was completely filled and built over during the 1970s–1990s. The area, now known for film studios and residential blocks, shows no remaining water surface. Its loss contributed to recurrent flooding in Kodambakkam during northeast monsoon.

properties.name: Virugambakkam Lake
properties.source: CMDA Master Plan / Care Earth Trust
properties.notes: Virugambakkam Lake has been reduced from ~150 ha to barely 12 ha. Encroachments from residential layouts, a bus terminus, and commercial establishments have consumed most of the water body. The remaining portion is highly polluted and no longer functionally useful for groundwater recharge.

properties.name: Pallikaranai Marsh
properties.source: Care Earth Trust / Ashoka Trust for Research in Ecology
properties.notes: Pallikaranai Marsh is one of India's most critically threatened wetlands. By the early 1990s — before the OMR IT corridor boom — the marsh covered ~2,500 ha (down from 5,000+ ha in the 1960s). It has since shrunk to ~320 ha due to IT park development (SIPCOT IT Park, Perungudi), the Perungudi garbage dump, and road construction. What remains is a Ramsar-recognised wetland and critical habitat for 115+ bird species, but drainage continues from all sides.

properties.name: Perungudi Lake
properties.source: Care Earth Trust / Greater Chennai Corporation records
properties.notes: Perungudi Lake was converted into one of Chennai's two major garbage dump sites in the 1980s. The 200-ha water body is now buried under decades of municipal waste. The site has been ordered to close by the National Green Tribunal but remediation is incomplete.

properties.name: Madipakkam Lake
properties.source: Madras High Court / NGT records on water body encroachments
properties.notes: Madipakkam Lake has lost 70% of its area to residential encroachments. Buildings have been constructed directly on the former lake bed. The remaining water body suffers from sewage inflow and is now largely stagnant. A case to restore the lake was filed at the Madras High Court.

properties.name: Sholinganallur Marshland
properties.source: Salim Ali Centre for Ornithology / Care Earth Trust
properties.notes: The Sholinganallur/Perumbakkam marshland along the OMR corridor covered ~600 ha of wetland habitat, distinct from (and south of) the main Pallikaranai marsh. IT park development from the late 1990s onward—including Tidel Park, DLF, and dozens of tech campuses—has reduced it to isolated patches. The area now experiences recurrent flooding during monsoon as the natural retention basin is gone.

properties.name: Villivakkam Lake
properties.source: CMDA / Revenue records / Care Earth Trust
properties.notes: Villivakkam Lake has been progressively encroached upon by residential layouts, a market complex, and bus stands. About 68% of the original area has been lost. The water quality of the remaining lake is severely degraded due to untreated sewage discharge from nearby localities.

properties.name: Kolathur Lake
properties.source: Care Earth Trust water body inventory
properties.notes: Kolathur Lake has been encroached upon from all sides by residential development. What remains is a heavily polluted water body that periodically floods the surrounding area during heavy rains—a direct result of the loss of its natural water-holding capacity.

properties.name: Tambaram Tank
properties.source: Survey of India maps / Tamil Nadu PWD records
properties.notes: Tambaram Tank, which once served as a key water source and flood buffer for the Tambaram area, has shrunk by 90% due to encroachments from residential and commercial construction. The reduced water body is no longer capable of sustaining the aquifer recharge it historically provided.

properties.name: Manali Wetlands
properties.source: TNPCB / Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board reports
properties.notes: Manali wetlands, located near Chennai's northern industrial corridor, have been drastically reduced by petrochemical plants, fertiliser factories, and other heavy industry. The area receives industrial effluent discharge and the surviving wetland patches are among the most polluted in Chennai. The wetlands once buffered the Ennore Creek floodplain.

properties.name: Ennore Creek Wetlands
properties.source: Coastal Management Society / National Green Tribunal (Chennai)
properties.notes: Ennore Creek and its associated wetlands have been severely degraded by the expansion of the Ennore and Kamarajar ports, thermal power plants, and coal ash ponds. The NGT has repeatedly issued orders to halt further encroachment but enforcement has been partial. The estuary supports significant fisheries and migratory bird populations.

properties.name: Muttukadu Backwaters
properties.source: CMDA Coastal Regulation Zone / Care Earth Trust
properties.notes: Muttukadu backwaters are a tidal estuary and lagoon system on the East Coast Road. About 45% of the original area has been lost to resort construction, boat clubs, and residential development. CRZ violations have been documented by the Tamil Nadu Coastal Zone Management Authority. The surviving area is a popular tourism and eco-tourism destination.

properties.name: Chetpet Lake (Reduced)
properties.source: GCC / Care Earth Trust / Madras High Court order 2018
properties.notes: Chetpet Lake once covered ~45 ha in central Chennai. It has been reduced to a small remnant of ~6 ha by road construction, encroachments, and the widening of Poonamallee High Road. A 2018 Madras High Court order mandated the GCC to restore and beautify the surviving portion; a partial restoration was completed but the lost area was not recovered.
